Assessor’s Office
The Assessors' Office and the Board of Assessors are responsible for determining the full
and fair cash value of all real and personal property in the City of Peabody and the
administration of Massachusetts General Laws relating to municipal finance and taxation.
978-538-5716
City Hall - 1st Floor
Auditing Department
Provides the Peabody City Council with an independent and objective assessment of all
municipal operations and financial processes in accordance with applicable auditing
standards.
978-538-5715
City Hall - 2nd Floor
Building Department
Administers and enforces the State Building Code and all other related work required to
inspect and permit construction work within the City of Peabody.
978-538-5786
City Hall - 1st Floor
Cemetery Department
Oversees the City’s municipal cemeteries. Maintains records, grounds, and equipment,
and assists with burial plot purchases.
978-531-1073
100 Rear Cedar Grove Ave
City Clerk’s Office
The City Clerk is the official record keeper for the City of Peabody. Records kept by the City
Clerk’s Office include vital statistics (including birth, marriage, and death), City Council
documents, and election records.
978-538-5756
City Hall - 1st Floor
Collector’s Office
Collects taxes as well as fields questions for all City taxes, which include real estate,
personal property, water/sewer, and motor vehicle excise taxes.
978-538-5748
City Hall - 1st Floor
Community Development
Leads the community’s vision by coordinating sustainable development, natural resource
stewardship, economic vitality, and people-centered transportation through obtaining
grants and administering fair and reasonable government regulations based on short- and
long-range planning.
978-538-5772
City Hall - 1st Floor
Conservation Commission
The Peabody Conservation Commission is composed of nine volunteer members, appointed by the Mayor. The Commission was established to protect and promote Peabody's natural resources, to protect watershed resources, to protect wetland resource areas, to provide permitting review for proposed projects within resource areas and their buffers, and to coordinate with other town officials and boards on conservation issues that relate to its areas of responsibility.
978-538-5782
City Hall - 1st Floor
Department of Public Services (DPS)
Oversees the City’s public works and water utility systems, ensuring the safe and reliable
operation of roadways, drainage networks, water supply, and wastewater collection.
978-536-0600
50 Farm Ave
Facilities Department
Manages and maintains a diverse portfolio of municipal buildings and grounds essential to
City operations. The department is responsible for more than 2 million square feet of
building space and over 1,100 acres of land, encompassing more than 55 City-owned
facilities.
978-536-7116
50 Farm Ave
Farms (Brooksby and Tillie’s)
Enhances quality of life in the City of Peabody through the stewardship of City-owned
farms, preservation of open space, and promotion of local agriculture, sustainability, and
community engagement.
Brooksby Farm Website
Tillie's Farm Website
Finance and Administration Department
Responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and administration of the City’s
financial management functions.
978-538-5711
City Hall - 2nd Floor
George Peabody House and Leatherworkers Museum
Collects, preserves, and interprets the life and legacy of philanthropist and native son
George Peabody.
978-278-5133
205 Washington St
Health Department
Promotes the health and well-being of residents of (and visitors to) Peabody through the
provision of school health services, public immunization clinics, communicable disease
follow-up, health education, public health emergency response, and the permitting and
inspection of facilities.
978-538-5926
City Hall - Ground Floor
Human Resources Department
Provides centralized human resources services including recruitment, benefits
administration, labor relations support, and employment compliance for the City of
Peabody’s municipal workforce. Partners with City leadership and departments to support
effective workforce management while promoting fair, consistent, and legally compliant
employment practices.
978-538-5723
City Hall - 2nd Floor
Information Technology Department
Serves as a strategic partner to all City agencies and departments by delivering innovative,
secure, and reliable technological solutions. Provides leadership in technology planning,
implementation, and governance to ensure systems and services align with the City’s
				operational goals and long-term vision.
Delivers dependable infrastructure, enterprise applications, cybersecurity, data
management, and technical support services that enable daily operations, regulatory
compliance, and informed decision-making. By maintaining scalable, secure, and resilient
systems, ensures continuity of services and positions the City to adapt to evolving
technological demands and community needs.
City Hall - Ground Floor
Library
The Peabody Institute Library is a historic, three-branch public library system that provides
Peabody residents with free access to books, technology, educational programs, and
cultural resources that support lifelong learning and community engagement.
978-531-0100
82 Main St
Mayor’s Office
As Chief Executive Officer of the City of Peabody, the Mayor implements the City’s strategic
vision, oversees the budget, serves as Chairperson ex-officio of the School Committee,
and promotes a thriving, equitable, and inclusive place to live, learn, visit, and do business.
The Mayor’s Office staff supports the Mayor in day-to-day operations and strategic
initiatives.
978-538-5702
City Hall - 2nd Floor
McVann O’Keefe Skating Rink
The James McVann-Louis O’Keefe Skating Rink provides a wide variety of recreational ice-
skating programs for the community at affordable prices.
978-535-2110
511 Lowell St
Municipal Security Department
Provides comprehensive safety and security oversight for City-owned properties,
personnel, and members of the public. Operates with a proactive, risk-based approach,
focused on prevention, mitigation, preparedness, and coordinated response.
978-538-5775
City Hall - Ground Floor
North Shore Children’s Museum
Brings children, families, and the community together through accessible, hands-on
learning experiences that use the power of play to spark curiosity, creativity, and early
childhood development.
978-538-5765
10 Main St
Parks, Recreation, and Forestry
Enhances quality of life in the City of Peabody through the stewardship of parks, public
spaces, urban forests, and recreational programs for residents of all ages.
978-536-7130
50 Farm Ave
Peabody Council on Aging
The Peabody Council on Aging (PCOA) addresses real concerns of our aging population by
providing social services, nutrition, transportation, engaging classes, programs, and
activities as well as offering volunteer opportunities. Operates a licensed Adult Day Health
site to support participants that need medical assistance to attend a program outside of
their home.
978-531-2254
79 Central St
Peabody Fire Department
Promotes the safety and protection of residents of (and visitors to) Peabody through
fire suppression, emergency medical response, rescue operations, fire prevention and
inspection services, public safety education, and preparedness for natural and man-made emergencies.
978-531-2200
47 Lowell St
Peabody Municipal Light Plant (PMLP)
A not-for-profit electric utility owned by their customers. PMLP is dedicated to providing
safe, reliable electricity and high-quality service to customers at the lowest possible rates.
978-531-5975
201 Warren St Ext
Peabody Police Department
Protects and serves the community by safeguarding lives and property, enforcing laws, and
reducing crime.
978-531-1212
Peabody Police Website
Purchasing Department
Sources various goods and outside services for support of departmental operations and
their service delivery to City residents. Responsible for finding qualified contractors to
perform construction and repair of our buildings, public works, and non-building site
projects.
978-538-5902
City Hall - Ground Floor
Retirement Department
The Retirement Board provides accurate and timely guidance regarding retirement
regulations and benefits to members and their beneficiaries. The retirement system is
funded by an annual appropriation from the City, employee contributions, and
investments.
978-538-5719
City Hall - Ground Floor
School Department
Peabody Public Schools’ mission is to prepare each student to reach his or her full intellectual, creative and individual potential through a fully integrated and diverse curriculum to meet the responsibilities of citizenship.
978-531-1600
Peabody Schools Website
Social Services and Behavioral Health Department
Supports the mental and physical health of Peabody residents through primary prevention,
intervention, referrals to treatments, and ongoing client support delivered through a team
of clinicians and care coordinators.
978-538-6339
6 Allens Ln
The Meadow at Peabody Golf Course
Provides a public golfing venue and recreational opportunity to both residents and non-
residents.
978-532-9390
Golf Course Website
Treasurer’s Office
Receives and disburses City funds, negotiates borrowing, and acts as custodian for City
monies.
978-538-5760
City Hall - 1st Floor
Veterans Services Department
Provides services for veterans and their dependents that may include applying for benefits
(both state and federal), helping with applications for VA medical care and services,
helping in employment and underemployment situations along with monetary support (if
qualified under the State 115 benefit program).
978-538-5925
City Hall - Ground Floor
Water Billing
978-536-7149
50 Farm Ave
City Hall
978-538-5900
24 Lowell St. Peabody, MA. 01960
